summary: When items bulk-set --apply stops early on an exhausted 429, it must persist which item IDs it already wrote (keyed by a signature of collection + --match + --set) so a re-run of the identical command skips those and reaches the untouched tail, instead of reselecting the same sorted head of the batch from the unchanged local mirror.
reason: The local mirror this command selects from is opened read-only and is never updated after a write, so a bare re-run after a rate-limit stop reselects the exact same sorted matched list from scratch. Without tracking what was already applied, the re-run burns rate-limit budget resending writes to items that already succeeded and can make zero net forward progress on the remaining items if the per-minute cap is tight enough. The fix adds a small sidecar JSON file under the CLI's state dir (mirrors the teach command's existing pattern of a state-dir sidecar file) recording applied item IDs per signature. Two things a regen must preserve, both caught by review after the first pass: (1) already-applied IDs must be excluded from the matched set *before* the --limit window is chosen, not just skipped within it -- otherwise a batch larger than --limit gets permanently stuck reselecting the same already-done head across every re-run and the resume state gets cleared as if nothing remained; (2) the sidecar file holds every in-flight batch's state keyed by signature (a map, not a single record), because a second --match/--set batch on the same collection getting rate-limited before the first one resumes must not overwrite the first batch's progress. The 'Re-run to continue where this left off' message is only honest because of both of these.
validated_outcome: TestBulkSetResumeRoundTrip, TestBulkSetResumeClearIgnoresOtherSignature, and TestBulkSetResumeSaveDoesNotOverwriteOtherSignature confirm save/load/clear round-trips correctly and independently per signature; TestSelectBulkTargetsAdvancesPastSkippedWindow confirms a capped window advances onto untouched items instead of reselecting an already-applied head.
